newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude buoyed by Iraq, August tightness.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude buoyed by Iraq, August tightness.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were quiet on Monday as traders awaited August loading programmes, while cash markets and outright values gained on uncertainty over when Iraqi crude exports will resume, traders said.

While some business was being talked on physical markets little was being done. A late flurry of buying on Friday took care of immediate demand and with the first of the August loading programmes issued traders were planning for next month's business.
Just one Brent cargo, loading July 29-31, remains to turn wet from the paper chains while Statfjord and Forties were heard on offer on Monday.

Three Brents traded on Friday -- at three cents below August, three above, and at fixed price for a prompt loading cargo. The weaker prices, down from the +10 paid on Thursday, were reportedly stable around flat to August on Monday
Late month Ekofisk, Troll and Forties cargoes also moved on Friday, at steady differentials, reflecting the continued tightness in the crude market with Iraqi barrels still absent.

IPE Brent futures were up 30 cents at $18.40 a barrel at 1150 GMT as dealers worried the lack of any clear result to negotiations between Baghdad and the U.N. on the details of an aid plan meant further delays to crude exports.
The distribution deal has to be finalised before exports can start under the second term of the oil-for-food deal. Last exports were in late May.
First loading programmes indicated tighter North Sea supply in August than in July, as expected, due to maintenance.

Early schedules showed the Oseberg crude system loading 19.32 million barrels in August, down from 20.4 million in July, while Norway's Statfjord will load 28 855,000 barrel cargoes, including two held over from July.
"Everything has firmed up a little this morning," said one broker. "It's partly the indication of reduced volumes of loading programmes but the U.N. and Iraq is the important one."
Inter-month spreads on the cash market firmed, with Aug/Sept moving from -0.09/-0.06 to -0.04/-0.02 and Sep/Oct firming to -0.10/-0.06.
Short-term swaps were also stronger, with this week (July 15-18) traded at August -10 cents and September -13 cents.

Mediterranean crude markets continued paralysed by Turkey's tender for 300,000 tonnes worth of sour. Turkey's Tupras was said to be waiting for the last possible moment to announce its result in the hope of clarification of the Iraqi situation
